title: Practice 13: при, на поезде, в этом году

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Расспрашиваешь солдата, при ___ (какое обстоятельство, prep. pl.) он ранен.
exercises.why: **обстоятельство → обстоятельствах** (prep. pl.). Neuter, inanimate; nominative plural обстоятельства. Declines like DLI's окно — every plural form has the same endings (P. pl. окнах). Ending -о → -ах.  **какой → каких** (prep. pl., agreeing with обстоятельствах). Adjective type III, guttural (after г, к, х) — declines like DLI's русский (every form has the same endings, apart from the masculine nominative singular (and the inanimate accusative equal to it), which ends in -ой here, not -ий): P. русских. Ending -ие → -их.  Declension: sg. обстоятельство · обстоятельства · обстоятельству · обстоятельство · обстоятельством · обстоятельстве; pl. обстоятельства · обстоятельств · обстоятельствам · обстоятельства · обстоятельствами · обстоятельствах.  «For the dative and the prepositional plural there are two kinds of endings for each case: -ам, -ами, -ах after a hard, a sibilant or a guttural consonant; -ям, -ями, -ях after a soft consonant, a «ь» or a vowel. The formation of these cases does not depend upon the gender of the noun, but only upon the sound preceding the ending.» — DLI, Lessons 42–45.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending -ой if stressed: новый — молодой; русский — плохой, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.» «The adjective «большой» belongs to the guttural type, in spite of its -ш-: большого, большому, большим, о большом.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: И нельзя ему ни поправиться на ___ (лошадь, prep. sg.), ни кровь обтереть.
exercises.why: **лошадь → лошади** (prep. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -ь. Declines like DLI's часть — every singular form has the same endings (P. sg. части), except the accusative, which follows the animacy rule. Ending -ь → -и.  Declension: sg. лошадь · лошади · лошади · лошадь · лошадью · лошади; pl. лошади · лошадей · лошадям · лошадей · лошадьми · лошадях.  «Feminine nouns ending in -ь in the nominative singular have -и in the prepositional singular: тетрадь — в тетради, часть — о части, дверь — на двери.» — DLI, Lessons 16–17.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Греки в ___ (шестой век, prep. sg.) находили его весьма грубым.
exercises.why: **век → веке** (prep. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a consonant. Declines like DLI's дом — every singular form has the same endings (P. sg. доме). Ending — (no ending) → -е.  **шестой → шестом** (prep. sg. m., agreeing with веке). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новый (every form has the same endings, apart from the masculine nominative singular (and the inanimate accusative equal to it), which ends in -ой here, not -ый): P. новом. Ending -ой → -ом.  Declension: sg. век · века · веку · век · веком · веке; pl. века · веков · векам · века · веками · веках.  «The prepositional case is always used with a preposition. … The basic ending of the prepositional case singular is -е.» — DLI, Lessons 16–17.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending -ой if stressed: новый — молодой; русский — плохой, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.» «The adjective «большой» belongs to the guttural type, in spite of its -ш-: большого, большому, большим, о большом.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Как в ___ (такой год, prep. pl.)?
exercises.prompt: *Фёдор Достоевский, «Чужая жена и муж под кроватью»*
exercises.why: **год → летах** (prep. pl.). Masculine, inanimate; nominative plural годы. Declines like DLI's стол — every plural form has the same endings (P. pl. столах). The form changes by more than its ending, so no single ending is given — see the declension below.  **такой → таких** (prep. pl., agreeing with летах). Adjective type III, guttural (after г, к, х) — declines like DLI's русский (every form has the same endings, apart from the masculine nominative singular (and the inanimate accusative equal to it), which ends in -ой here, not -ий): P. русских. Ending -ие → -их.  Declension: sg. год · года · году · год · годом · годе; pl. годы · годов · годам · годы · годами · годах.  «For the dative and the prepositional plural there are two kinds of endings for each case: -ам, -ами, -ах after a hard, a sibilant or a guttural consonant; -ям, -ями, -ях after a soft consonant, a «ь» or a vowel. The formation of these cases does not depend upon the gender of the noun, but only upon the sound preceding the ending.» — DLI, Lessons 42–45.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending -ой if stressed: новый — молодой; русский — плохой, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.» «The adjective «большой» belongs to the guttural type, in spite of its -ш-: большого, большому, большим, о большом.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Во ___ (день, prep. sg.) адовом не будет хуже здешнего!
exercises.why: **день → дне** (prep. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in -ь. Declines like DLI's автомобиль — every singular form has the same endings (P. sg. автомобиле). Ending -ь → -е, with the fleeting -е- of the stem dropped: дн- + -е.  Declension: sg. день · дня · дню · день · днём · дне; pl. дни · дней · дням · дни · днями · днях.  «The prepositional case is always used with a preposition. … The basic ending of the prepositional case singular is -е.» — DLI, Lessons 16–17.  «Certain masculine nouns have the vowels е or о only in the nominative singular (and in the accusative if inanimate): отец — отца, американец — американца, кусок — куска, звонок — звонка.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: В ___ (сам конец, prep. sg.) декабря мы наконец приехали в Челябинск.
exercises.why: **конец → конце** (prep. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a consonant. Declines like DLI's дом — every singular form has the same endings (P. sg. доме). Ending — (no ending) → -е, with the fleeting -е- of the stem dropped: конц- + -е.  **сам → самом** (prep. sg. m., agreeing with конце). «сам» is a pronoun-type word with its own declension, not the regular adjective pattern, so no ending rule is claimed. Its forms (m. sg.): сам · самого · самому · сам (inan.) / самого (anim.) · самим · самом.
